**Analysis of test image:**
The test image shows a single young mango shoot/leaf that is:
- Curved into a crescent/C-shape
- Yellowish-green base color
- Brown irregular necrotic lesions/patches scattered along the surface
- Still retaining its overall shape (not stripped or bare)

**Ruling out candidates:**
- **Cutting_Weevil**: Reference shows bare stripped stems with only triangular leaf remnants — very different from the intact leaf shape in test image
- **Die_Back**: Reference shows fully brown/dead, completely necrotic curled leaves — more severe than test image
- **Gall_Midge**: Shows round blister galls on mature green leaves — not matching
- **Bacterial_Canker**: Angular necrosis on leaf margins of mature leaves — not matching
- **Sooty_Mould**: Black coating on surfaces — not matching
- **Powdery_Mildew**: White powdery spots — not matching

**Best match — Anthracnose:**
The Anthracnose reference (top-left panel) shows a very similar young mango leaf with brownish necrotic lesions, curled shape, on a yellowish-green young flush. The symptom description mentions "semicircular lesions on margins of young leaves" which aligns with the brown patches visible on this young shoot.
